title.narrative: South Asia Subregional Economic Cooperation National Single Window Project

description.narrative: The project will leverage information and communication technology to improve efficiency in cross-border control procedures. It will support the development of an automated system that will enable sharing of harmonized data across systems of cross-border regulatory agencies, Maldives Ports Limited, and Maldives Airports Company Limited. It will also allow traders and other service providers to submit, and to obtain unified clearance of, export and import documentation requirements through a single point of entry. The report also describes a technical assistance that will support the Government of Maldives in related capacity development of various stakeholders, including on change management.

Output: Indicator Indicator: NSW system commissioned and maintained with at least 80% of service level standards achieved Progress/Status: Tradian Phase 1, which covered 19 out of 25 key functions/modules envisaged for Tradian platform, went live in April 2025, initially operating alongside existing service delivery mechanisms. Following a successful stabilization period completed on 21 September 2025, Tradian is now the exclusive channel for Phase 1 services. This marks a major milestone in modernizing trade-related service delivery in Maldives, enabling online registration of key trade related documents, streamlining cargo and vessel declarations, and integrating seamlessly with the relevant information communication technology (ICT) systems. As of 1 October 2025, Tradian has onboarded 65 shipping agents, 84 freight forwarders, 8 importers/exporters, and has processed 117 vessel registrations, as well as received 48 Estimated Time of Arrival submissions and registered 1,784 Bills of Lading.
Tradian Phase 2 marks the final rollout of Tradian, driving full integration with customs, airport, and other regulatory agency systems to advance trade facilitation. Development was previously delayed due to data privacy concerns raised by MCS, which were resolved in June 2025 following the government's adoption of a “Hybrid Model.” Under this model, Tradian receives trader declarations, stores only minimal header-level data in NSW, and transmits complete data to MCS for processing within its proprietary UNCTAD-based systems. Data Source: Ministry of Economic Development Report Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2026 Target value: 80

Output: National Single Window system for international trade and reengineered trade processes established. Indicator: NSW legal framework to enable electronic service delivery through NSW finalized and submitted to Parliament Progress/Status: MoEDT led and completed the preliminary legal framework drafting for enabling trade related service delivery through NSW. However, considering the larger goals and ambitions of the Maldives Government towards achieving Maldives 2.0 (an initiative for Government wide transformation of public service delivery), Government is currently expanding the scope of the preliminary NSW legal framework to address the larger Digital Service Delivery goals and requirements as a whole at Government level. Drafting of such expanded legislative framework (referred as Maldives Digital Services Bill) is anchored by the NCIT under MoHST. NCIT completed drafting the new MDS Bill, which is currently undergoing legal review within the MoHST. After such review, the bill will be circulated among other Government stakeholders for consultation. Tentatively, such consultation is planned for conclusion in August 2025, after which the bill will be submitted to the Attorney General's Office (AGO) for its review and finalization for submission to the President's Office and to the Parliament. This entire procedure, including review and finalization at AGO, the President's office and the Parliament is expected to take a few more months. This bill is envisaged to play a key role in providing the legal backbone for Maldives 2.0, which is expected to overhaul and enhance the country's public service delivery and governance through digital platforms. The World Bank is also assisting the Government in drafting the MDS Bill.
Personal Data Protection Bill. This bill was developed following Cabinet's directive, aimed at addressing data security and privacy in connection with the MDS Bill. It was submitted to AGO around February 2025 and is being finalized for submission to the President. At the President's Office, a political and policy-level review will be undertaken. Based on precedents, no substantial modifications are anticipated during this process. Upon President's clearance, the bill will be tabled in Parliament, followed by a brief period of public consultation. Once this process is complete, the legislation will proceed to formal approval and implementation. MoHST is targeting to submit the data protection bill in the upcoming parliamentary session this August.
